notice: Original JARVIS reference notes, not a complete copy of the Blender manual. Version-sensitive APIs must be checked against the installed Blender version. Recipe and artistic advice are starting points, not guarantees of quality.

cards.title: Start with a brief and measurable acceptance checks
cards.tags: planning workflow reference silhouette dimensions scale units blockout
cards.body: Record the intended object, dimensions, audience, realism target, output format and performance budget. Separate silhouette, proportions, construction details, materials and presentation. Establish metric units and reference dimensions before detailing. Block out and inspect front/side/perspective views first. Save incremental versions in a project workspace. A successful operation is not evidence of a good result: inspect the render, dimensions and exported artifact. For unfamiliar requests retrieve relevant cards, make a plan and identify unsupported operations before touching the scene.

cards.title: Transforms, origins and predictable modifiers
cards.tags: scale rotation dimensions apply transform origin mirror bevel inconsistent
cards.body: Inspect object scale, local axes, dimensions and origin before diagnosing an uneven bevel, mirrored object or export. Apply scale only when appropriate to the workflow; never blindly apply every transform on rigged or animated objects. Mirror needs a deliberate mirror plane or reference object. Check modifier order: it changes the evaluated geometry. Keep a non-destructive working object and export from a duplicate when destructive conversion is required.

cards.title: Hard-surface props and clean edge highlights
cards.tags: hard surface prop robot mechanical bevel boolean topology normals weighted panel enclosure
cards.body: Block out major volumes and negative spaces first. Use Mirror for symmetry and Boolean for purposeful cutouts; inspect the resulting topology before subdivision or deformation. Give real edges a small bevel so lighting can reveal them. Set bevel width relative to real object size, clamp overlap and inspect intersections. More segments do not fix bad proportions. Shading corrections cannot repair overlapping or non-manifold geometry. Validate normals and bevel artifacts under a grazing key light.

cards.title: Subdivision and topology
cards.tags: subdivision topology support loop crease pinching smooth organic quad poles
cards.body: Use a low-resolution control cage and enough supporting structure to preserve the silhouette. Subdivision smooths existing topology; it does not invent a well-designed surface. Place poles away from high-curvature/deformation areas, inspect pinching and avoid unnecessary density. Start with low viewport levels and increase only when the camera reveals faceting. Keep render subdivision within the memory budget; doubling subdivision can sharply increase face counts.

cards.title: Realistic humans: assets, sculpting and retopology
cards.tags: human character avatar face anatomy realistic makehuman mpfb skin retopology sculpt likeness
cards.body: Begin with a properly licensed anatomical base or carefully constructed sculpt, not a collection of primitive limbs. Match proportions from suitable reference views. A single photograph does not provide accurate hidden geometry or medical measurements. Separate high-resolution sculpt, retopologized deformation mesh and baked detail. Design edge flow around eyes, mouth, shoulders and hips; test expressions and bent poses. Skin, eyes, hair, clothing and lighting are separate quality requirements. Record licenses and source files for every imported asset.

cards.title: PBR materials and Principled BSDF
cards.tags: pbr materials texture shader principled roughness metallic normal srgb non color fabric skin leather metal
cards.body: Use Principled BSDF as a consistent physically based starting point. Base-color images normally carry color information; roughness, metallic and normal maps are data and need the appropriate non-color interpretation. Route tangent-space normal maps through a Normal Map node. Match texture scale to object size and UVs. Metallic and roughness describe different properties; dark diffuse paint is not automatically metal. Subtle roughness variation often adds more credibility than excessive bump. Test with neutral illumination before judging stylized lighting.

cards.title: UV unwrap, texel density and baking
cards.tags: uv unwrap texture seam baking normal ao texel density checker overlapping padding
cards.body: Place seams deliberately, use a checker texture to find stretching and maintain a sensible texel density between visible parts. Leave padding between islands for filtered textures and mipmaps. Mirrored/overlapping UVs may be useful but are not appropriate for every bake. When baking high to low, verify the target UV map, active image, object selection, cage/ray distance and normal convention. Inspect the baked result on the final low-resolution material before discarding any source.

cards.title: Detailed garments, seams, folds and cloth
cards.tags: clothes clothing garment shirt skirt dress fabric cloth sewing seam folds solidify collision
cards.body: Model a garment with intentional silhouette, construction seams and appropriate ease around the body. Add thickness with a suitable mesh or Solidify workflow and inspect cuffs, hems and intersections. Cloth simulation needs adequate topology, collision setup and scale; use low-cost tests before a full cache. Folds should follow tension, compression, gravity and seam placement rather than random noise. Use separate fabric-scale normal/roughness detail. Test the garment on bent poses; a convincing still image is not proof of animation-ready fit.

cards.title: Hair curves and grooming
cards.tags: hair hairstyle curves groom scalp eyebrows beard density clump
cards.body: Use the hair-curves workflow or licensed groom assets suitable for the target renderer. Establish the scalp attachment, parting, hairline and large clumps before adding fine strands. Check silhouette from several angles and keep density appropriate for the camera distance. Hair cards may suit a real-time destination better than dense render hair. Confirm exporter support; unsupported curves must be converted or replaced deliberately, not assumed to export unchanged.

cards.title: Rigging, weights and deformation tests
cards.tags: rigging armature bones weights skinning pose rigify deformation shoulder elbow knee
cards.body: Use a clean rest pose and a deliberate bone hierarchy. Automatic weights are an initial estimate, not a finished rig. Test elbows, knees, shoulders, wrists and hips at meaningful angles; inspect collapsing volumes and leaking weights. Use corrective shapes or topology changes where necessary. Keep control rigs separate from export/deform requirements. Rigify availability depends on the installed extension/version: detect it before claiming it exists or downloading it. Verify the intended target application's bone and animation conventions.

cards.title: Animation, natural poses and turntables
cards.tags: animation keyframe timing spacing action fcurve interpolation turntable walk idle pose
cards.body: Set frame rate and duration before animation. Block the main poses and timing, then refine spacing, arcs and secondary motion. Natural balance needs a believable center of mass and contacts; random bone motion is not a walk cycle. Use linear interpolation for a constant-speed turntable and intentional easing for character movement. Inspect the first/last frame for loop discontinuity. Preview a low-cost playblast before final renders and verify frame range, action assignment and exported playback.

cards.title: Studio lighting and camera composition
cards.tags: lighting camera render studio key fill rim three point shadow focal length product
cards.body: Start with a neutral key light, restrained fill and deliberate background separation. Large area lights produce broad highlights useful for reading shape; move lights before increasing power blindly. Watch contact shadows and avoid a subject that appears to float. Choose focal length and camera distance to control perspective instead of distorting the model to fit the frame. Use neutral lighting for asset evaluation and a separate presentation setup for style. Check multiple views, especially on reflective materials.

cards.title: Cycles, EEVEE, noise and color management
cards.tags: render cycles eevee gpu optix cuda samples denoise fireflies agx color management noise black
cards.body: Choose the renderer for the deliverable: a fast interactive preview and a high-quality final may use different settings. Confirm actual GPU device availability instead of assuming a GPU is enabled. Reduce image size and samples while iterating. Denoising cannot restore detail lost to inadequate sampling or bad lighting. Check exposure, display/view transform and output format before altering textures. Distinguish material problems from display-management problems. Render a small region or frame before starting an expensive sequence.

cards.title: Geometry Nodes for reusable procedural assets
cards.tags: geometry nodes procedural scatter instancing realization seed sockets repeat distribution
cards.body: Expose a small set of meaningful controls such as dimensions, density and seed. Keep instances while possible to reduce memory; realize them only when the next operation or destination needs actual geometry. Check source geometry attributes, spaces and domains. Use deterministic seeds when repeatability matters. Cache or bake only after verifying the supported workflow for the installed version. Do not assume every procedural node graph becomes an equivalent editable graph in glTF or another application.

cards.title: GLB/glTF export and mobile performance
cards.tags: export glb gltf web mobile threejs vrm texture compression drawcall materials mesh lod
cards.body: Treat export as a separate verification stage. Confirm intended objects, transforms, skinning, animation range, UVs and supported material channels. Procedural Blender shaders are not guaranteed to become equivalent glTF materials; bake or simplify deliberately. Limit excessive mesh density, material slots and texture sizes for phones. Export to a new workspace filename and reopen it in the actual target viewer. Check orientation, scale, missing textures, transparency and animation. A file existing on disk does not prove visual correctness.

cards.title: 3D printing and dimension checks
cards.tags: 3d print printing stl manufacturing manifold watertight wall thickness tolerances units
cards.body: Set actual units and dimensions before export. Inspect non-manifold edges, inverted faces, self-intersections and enclosed loose parts. Wall thickness, tolerances and support requirements depend on the printer, material and process; do not invent universal values. Verify dimensions again in the slicer. Keep an editable source and export a separate manufacturing copy. A manifold mesh alone does not establish structural safety or printability.

cards.title: bpy scripting, context failures and safe execution
cards.tags: python bpy api script context poll failed operators background threading data automation
cards.body: Prefer explicit bpy.data datablock access for predictable scripts where practical. bpy.ops often depends on the active scene, editor, mode and selection; diagnose poll/context errors rather than retrying identical calls. Query bpy.app.version and available RNA properties before using version-sensitive features. Blender API calls belong on Blender's main thread; external socket threads should queue work for its timer/main loop. Never run unreviewed downloaded scripts, arbitrary model-generated exec, shell commands or filesystem access as a workaround. Use typed tools, bounded outputs and explicit workspace paths.

cards.title: Fast troubleshooting without random retries
cards.tags: troubleshooting invisible black pink missing texture normals clipping memory crash slow failed
cards.body: Diagnose one class at a time: object hidden/excluded, wrong active camera, clipping range, normals, missing image path, material assignment, render engine and color management. A pink material usually calls for checking missing image dependencies. A slow scene calls for measured subdivision, instances, texture memory, samples and modifier cost. Read the actual error and compare against versioned references. If a window method fails, use an existing compatible typed MCP operation; do not claim an unsupported operation was solved. Stop on uncertain writes and preserve the working file.
